Target: 3 years 15 https://www.porttb.com/tariff-information Page46 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version 4 TECHNICAL DETAILS The total liquid CO storage capacity of 30,000 m³ is provided by 11 insulated horizontal pressure vessels 2 (each with a diameter of 10 m and a length of 32.3 m). This accommodates one full 20,000 m³ tanker and a buffer volume of 10,000 m³ equal to 50% of a tanker load or approximately 1.5 days production at the design rate. The project is targeting a tanker turnaround time of 24 hours (inclusive of a non-loading time of 6 hours for mooring operations etc.) which sets the loading pump capacity of 1,250 m³/h. With this configuration the system should be able to load a 20,000 m3 tanker in approximately 16 hours. To provide redundancy, 2×100% loading pumps are provided (one in operation and one as a spare). The export system also includes a metering package for liquid CO pumped to the vessel, and CO gas returning from the vessel. 2 2 Three loading arms are provided for the following services:  Offloading Liquefied CO (LCO ) 2 2  CO vapor return 2  Spare arm capable of either service 4.1 CO CONDITIONS AT RECEIPT AND DELIVERY 2 There are no CCS projects known as of this writing in the Tampa Bay area that are far enough along to have established a quality or condition specification. Aptamus is in contact with several emitters who are considering carbon capture installations at their Tampa-area facilities. But none are prepared to establish quality specifications, or even the general condition (pressure and temperature) yet. In the meantime, for our planning purposes, we have assumed that the CO will be processed by the emitter to the same quality 2 standard as that required by the Northern Lights project in Norway, which is summarized in Table 4.1. As such, there is no significant purification equipment intended to be installed at T-RICH. If measurement devices at T-RICH detect incoming CO that is out of spec, the T-RICH operators will instruct the emitter 2 to stop sending captured CO down the pipeline, valves will be closed, the pipeline will be vented and 2 purged (potentially through the vent stack on site, or back to the emitter), and the equipment at T-RICH will be idled until the emitter can improve the quality of its outgoing CO . 2 The CO supply to the plant through the pipeline is assumed to come from amine-based post-combustion 2 carbon capture technology applied to natural gas-fired equipment. The removal of nitrogen oxides (NOx) and sulfur oxides (SOx) is typically part of the operations at upstream carbon capture plants that use amine-based processes.
